data.one_liner: Peer-to-peer connectivity and nearby device discovery for Android and iOS
data.what_it_does: Enables peer-to-peer communication and discovery of nearby devices on Android and iOS using Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Supports advertising, browsing, streaming data, messages, and resource sharing.
use_when: You need local peer-to-peer data sharing without internet access
You are building an offline multiplayer game or local collaboration app for Android and iOS
avoid_when: You need standard server-client cloud communication over the internet
You are testing on Android emulators (real devices are required)
strengths: Cross-platform support for Android (Nearby Connections API / Wi-Fi P2P) and iOS (Multipeer Connectivity)
Supports message-based data, streaming, and resource files over UDP
weaknesses: Android emulators are not supported; requires real devices for testing
Requires platform-specific configuration and permissions on iOS
data.setup_notes: Requires native configuration on iOS 14+ including NSBonjourServices, UIRequiresPersistentWiFi, and NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription keys in Info.plist.
